title: Acyclic-resolution comparison for underlying abelian sheaves of prime modules
statement: Let $i:Y\to X$ be a scheme morphism [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and $r$ prime. Suppose the restriction on global sections is an isomorphism for every $\mathbf F_r$-module-valued etale sheaf on $X$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Suppose that for every injective such sheaf $J$, the underlying abelian sheaf of $i^{-1}J$ has zero cohomology in all positive degrees [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. Then for every module-valued sheaf $M$ on $X$ and every $q\geq0$, the canonical pullback on abelian cohomology of the underlying abelian sheaf $U(M)$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], $H^q(X,U(M))\to H^q(Y,i^{-1}U(M))$, is bijective [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback].

source.place: Second and third steps of the parent proof; Tag 095T second paragraph and Tag 03FD

proof.text: Choose an injective resolution of the given module-valued sheaf; forgetting coefficients is exact. Its underlying terms are acyclic on X by 03FD. Exact inverse image, commuting with forgetting, gives a resolution with acyclic terms on Y by the hypothesis. Leray computes both abelian cohomologies from their section complexes. Enough injectives for ModuleCat-valued etale sheaves is available from the Grothendieck abelian instances; no conversion of an arbitrary annihilated sheaf is part of this statement.

The degree-zero assumption makes the section-complex restriction an isomorphism termwise, so its homology maps are bijective, including degree zero. Compare with abelian injective resolutions on X and Y. Naturality gives the commuting square of section complexes, and homotopy uniqueness identifies its map with the canonical Ext pullback cohomologyMap, including the constant-integer-sheaf comparison. No K-injective or unbounded resolution is necessary.
